name: Tycho active-abstraction quick-death model
purpose: A bounded Pass 63 Stable combat experiment that preserves G0031 aim/fire authority and invokes a typed lifecycle world model only after a verified sub-30-second death.

paper.adaptation: partial stochastic lifecycle model; not a claim of deterministic game simulation

functions.init: previous rendered life duration plus bounded quick-death streak
functions.transition: classify one life boundary and update the hidden streak
functions.outcome: interrupt spawn cascades while preserving confirmed-target engagement
functions.metareasoning: bypass on ordinary lives; use only after a verified quick death; invalidate on target, damage, death, or match end

knownFailureReferences: Always-on respawn escape had isolated wins but failed replication.
Quick-death adaptation layered over an always-on base path did not pass promotion gates.
This candidate therefore sets the base escape to zero and uses the model only when the compact life-boundary abstraction is supported.

evaluation.promotionRule: Three consecutive valid passing repetitions with model-use attribution and zero retained regressions.

rollback.disable: PROGRAMMATIC_WORLD_MODEL=false and restore all G0031 values
